content.text: Diloti (Î”Î·Î»Ï‰Ï„Î®, from the verb Î´Î·Î»ÏŽÎ½Ï‰ meaning 'to declare') is the most popular and complex Greek fishing game. It combines mechanics from Kontsina and Xeri with a 'declaration' (build) system inspired by Casino. Players capture cards by matching or summing values, protected by declarations that define specific capture sets.

Diloti originated in Greece and is a cornerstone of Greek coffee-shop (kafeneio) gaming culture. It evolved by merging older fishing games (Kontsina) with matching bonuses (Xeri) and strategic declarations.
52 cards. Aces rank as 1 for sums, but otherwise have high point value.
6 cards per player; 4 face-up on table. If 3 or 4 face cards of same value are on the table, it's a misdeal.

items.text: Long Game Target: Use 121 points instead of 61 as the game target.
Forced Capture: If a played card can capture, the play must include a legal capture rather than laying.
Three Face Cards Keep: When initial table cards include exactly three equal face cards, keep deal and allow capture by the fourth matching face card.
